question: A table has a marked price of 8,000. A shopkeeper purchased it at two successive discounts of 20% and 25%. He sold the table for Rs. 8,000 after spending 300 on transportation. Find his profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discounts of 20% and 25% equal a single equivalent discount of 40%.

Initial Cost Price = 60% of ₹8000 = ₹4800.

Total Cost Price = Initial CP + Transportation = 4800 + 300 = ₹5100.

Profit = Selling Price − Total Cost Price = 8000 − 5100 = ₹2900.

Profit % = (2900 ÷ 5100) × 100 = 2900 ÷ 51 = 56 ⁴⁴/₅₁%.

**∴ The correct answer is 56 ⁴⁴/₅₁%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹8,000

Successive discounts = 20% and 25%

Transportation cost = ₹300

Selling Price (SP) = ₹8,000

**Formula Used:**

Total CP = Initial CP + Overhead expenses

Profit = SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

 
 Marked Price (MP) = ₹8000

 
• 
 

 Discount = 40% (₹3200)

 
 Initial CP = ₹4800

 
 Transport = ₹300
 
 +

 
• 
 

 
 Total CP = ₹5100

 
 Profit = ₹2900

 +

 Final Selling Price (SP) = ₹8000
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Cost Price = 8000 × (100 − 20)/100 × (100 − 25)/100

⇒ Initial Cost Price = 8000 × (80 ÷ 100) × (75 ÷ 100)

⇒ Initial Cost Price = 8000 × (4 ÷ 5) × (3 ÷ 4) = ₹4,800

⇒ Total Cost Price = 4800 + 300 = ₹5,100

⇒ Profit = Selling Price − Total Cost Price

⇒ Profit = 8000 − 5100 = ₹2,900

⇒ Profit % = (2900 ÷ 5100) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 2900 ÷ 51 = 56 ⁴⁴/₅₁%

**∴ The correct answer is 56 ⁴⁴/₅₁%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts of x% and y% are given successively, the single equivalent discount percentage is given by [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

Effective Cost Price

The total effective Cost Price is always calculated by adding all overhead expenses (such as transportation, repairs, and installation) to the initial purchasing price.

Profit Calculation Base

Profit and Loss percentages are mathematically evaluated on the Total Cost Price uniformly, unless explicitly stated to be evaluated on the Selling Price.
